description:
Backend-impl slice of JMAP-g7wu.2.4: implement AddRole/RemoveRole/UpdateRole and AddMember/RemoveMember/UpdateMember variants in MemoryBackend::apply_space_patch.

Cross-cutting concern: role-hierarchy enforcement.
- Members may only add/modify roles whose 'position' is strictly less than their own highest-position role (draft §Space/set lines 1096, 1102).
- This check spans BOTH role and member ops (a member-add with role_ids has to verify the caller can grant those roles).

Cascading semantics for RemoveRole:
- Members holding ONLY the removed role(s) are demoted to @everyone (draft line 1099).
- Iterate space.members; for each, intersect their role_ids with the removed set; if the result is empty, replace with @everyone.

ULID assignment for AddRole: generate new RoleId using same ULID source as Space/Message creation.

Depends on .4.1 (SpacePatchOp enum) landing. Parallelizable with .4.4 (channels) and .4.5 (categories) — different match arms in the same apply_space_patch fn.
notes:
Decision (2026-05-11, Mark): re-scoped per JMAP-ga0q approval. Foundation `JmapBackend::principal_id` resolves the identity blocker; `Space.owner_id` (JMAP-g7wu.2.4.11) resolves the owner-tracking blocker. This bead now lands the FULL backend implementation including role-hierarchy enforcement and owner protection — not just the mechanical slice.

## Re-scoped acceptance (replaces the prior 'mechanical-only slice' framing)

Backend implementation in MemoryBackend::apply_space_patch covering AddRole/RemoveRole/UpdateRole and AddMember/RemoveMember/UpdateMember variants, with:

  1. **Permission gating** — for each op, resolve caller's effective permissions via the caller's principal_id (Self::principal_id(caller)). Caller's permissions = union of permissions across all roles where role_id ∈ caller's space membership + @everyone defaults. Compare against required permissions from required_permissions_for_op (JMAP-g7wu.2.4.10).

  2. **Role-hierarchy enforcement** — per draft §Space/set lines 1096, 1102: members may only add/modify roles whose 'position' is strictly less than their own highest-position role. Backend reads caller's highest role position from Space.members and rejects ops referencing roles at or above that ceiling. Cross-cuts AddRole/UpdateRole AND AddMember/UpdateMember (the latter when role_ids contains a role above the caller's ceiling).

  3. **Owner protection** — RemoveMember on member where member.id == space.owner_id MUST reject. UpdateMember may modify the owner's nick or role_ids but cannot transfer ownership (Space/transferOwnership is reserved for future spec work).

  4. **Cascade semantics for RemoveRole** — members holding only removed roles are demoted to @everyone (draft line 1099). Iterate space.members; for each, intersect their role_ids with the removed set; if the result is empty, replace with @everyone.

  5. **ULID assignment for AddRole** — generate new RoleId using same source as Space/Message creation.

  6. **Whole-patch reject on permission failure** — if any op in the patch is forbidden, the WHOLE update for that Space id is rejected. Matches RFC 8620 /set atomicity for the affected update target.

  7. **Single-user mode handling** — when Self::principal_id(caller) returns None, the backend allows all ops without identity-dependent checks. Documented in MemoryBackend rustdoc as 'no-identity mode; not suitable for multi-user deployments'.

Estimated landing: ~600-800 LOC + tests including hierarchy/owner/cascade coverage.

## Updated dependencies

  - Depends on JMAP-g7wu.2.4.1 (SpacePatchOp enum — closed)
  - Depends on JMAP-ga0q.1 (foundation principal_id — open, blocks)
  - Depends on JMAP-g7wu.2.4.10 (required_permissions_for_op helper — open, blocks)
  - Depends on JMAP-g7wu.2.4.11 (Space.owner_id field — open, blocks)

## Supersedes

  - JMAP-g7wu.2.4.7 (handler-side permission gates) — closed as superseded; gates are backend-canonical per workspace policy from JMAP-ga0q.

Human label removed; the autonomous /do-beads loop can pick this up once all four dependencies land.
Design reversal (2026-05-12, Mark): the 2026-05-11 re-scope above is partially SUPERSEDED. Spec author has reversed the single-owner design — the JMAP Chat spec will NOT declare a normative `Space.ownerId` field; "who controls a Space" is implementation-defined / out-of-band. Workspace impl revert is tracked as JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12.

Updated acceptance criteria (replaces the 2026-05-11 "Re-scoped acceptance" block in the description above):

Backend implementation in MemoryBackend::apply_space_patch covering AddRole/RemoveRole/UpdateRole and AddMember/RemoveMember/UpdateMember variants, with:

  1. **Permission gating** — for each op, resolve caller's effective permissions via `Self::principal_id(caller)`. Caller's permissions = union of permissions across all SpaceRoles where role_id is in caller's `members[i].role_ids` + `@everyone` defaults. Compare against required permissions from `required_permissions_for_op` (JMAP-g7wu.2.4.10).

  2. **Role-hierarchy enforcement** — per draft §Space/set lines 1096, 1102: members may only add/modify roles whose `position` is strictly less than their own highest-position role. Backend reads caller's highest role position from `Space.members` and rejects ops referencing roles at or above that ceiling. Cross-cuts AddRole/UpdateRole AND AddMember/UpdateMember (the latter when `role_ids` contains a role above the caller's ceiling).

  3. **DROPPED — Owner protection.** The 2026-05-11 re-scope required "RemoveMember on member where member.id == space.owner_id MUST reject" and "Destroy requires caller == ownerId". Both are gone. The new posture: backend exposes server-extensible hooks but enforces no owner-keyed identity logic of its own.

     Replacement for "owner cannot be removed": expose a `MemoryBackend` config knob (e.g., `protect_last_admin: bool`, default `false` for backward compat with existing tests) that, when set, causes `RemoveMember` to reject if the removal would leave zero members holding any of `manage_members` / `manage_space`. The check is purely permission-graph-based; it does not reference a designated "owner". Document the knob's existence in MemoryBackend rustdoc and PLAN.md as "deployment-policy stand-in; production backends will replace this with their own last-admin protection logic."

     Replacement for "destroy requires owner identity": the `Space/destroy` path (NOT in this bead's variant set, but referenced for completeness) keeps requiring `manage_space` permission only. Stronger destroy authorization (multi-admin approval, designated controller, etc.) is server-defined and not enforced in MemoryBackend.

  4. **Cascade semantics for RemoveRole** — members holding only removed roles are demoted to `@everyone` (draft line 1099). Iterate `space.members`; for each, intersect their `role_ids` with the removed set; if the result is empty, replace with `@everyone`.

  5. **ULID assignment for AddRole** — generate new RoleId using same source as Space/Message creation.

  6. **Whole-patch reject on permission failure** — if any op in the patch is forbidden, the WHOLE update for that Space id is rejected. Matches RFC 8620 /set atomicity for the affected update target.

  7. **Single-user mode handling** — when `Self::principal_id(caller)` returns None, the backend allows all ops without identity-dependent checks. Documented in MemoryBackend rustdoc as "no-identity mode; not suitable for multi-user deployments."

## Updated dependencies

  - Depends on JMAP-g7wu.2.4.1 (SpacePatchOp enum — closed)
  - Depends on JMAP-g7wu.2.4.10 (required_permissions_for_op helper — closed)
  - Depends on JMAP-ga0q.1 (foundation principal_id — closed)
  - Depends on JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12 (revert workspace Space.ownerId impl — open) — must land BEFORE this bead can pick up, otherwise the backend would still have a stale `space.owner_id` field to reckon with.

The dep on JMAP-g7wu.2.4.11 (closed-superseded) is satisfied; left in place for history.

Estimated landing: ~600-800 LOC + tests including hierarchy / cascade / last-admin-protection coverage. Slightly smaller than the 2026-05-11 estimate since owner-protection logic is gone.
De-labelling human per JMAP-tqhv recommendation (2026-05-12): blocker JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12 (Space.ownerId revert) closed, bead's 2026-05-12 re-scoped acceptance is concrete enough to claim. Tracked under JMAP-v9py compliance sweep.
